That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity. The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves. But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December. How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis It is hard not to pick the Jaguars here, and they once again get a clean sweep. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team. The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore. Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud. The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense. The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years. According to NextGenStats, Jacksonville has generated a 39.6% pressure rate this season (8th-highest), and its pressures have arrived in 2.43 seconds on average, the quickest in the NFL. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most. This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13. On the positive side, the Ravens will be playing in front of their home crowd. However, they are going to be playing without superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup signal caller Tyler Huntley. Getting the start will be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. He came into the game last week against the Buffalo Bills and made his NFL debut, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Hailing from Boston College, the 6-foot-3 and 225-pound quarterback threw for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just one interception in 2025 with the Huskies. He completed 69 percent of his passes that year and chipped in with 131 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Behind Fagnano, the team will have Kedon Slovis as the primary backup. He was signed off of the Green Bay Packers' practice squad this week. Baltimore has made the move to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, but that trade will not finalize until later in the week. He won't be eligible to play against the Jaguars. Just hours before the game against Jacksonville kicks off, the Ravens have been slammed with a horrific prediction. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio isn't giving Baltimore any chance to knock off the 5-2 Jaguars. He is predicting that the Ravens will be defeated by a final score of 27-13. At the end of the day, Baltimore has a lot of adversity to overcome. Sometimes, teams find the best of themselves in these moments. But, there is no question that the Ravens are facing an uphill battle against one of the top contenders in the AFC. Coming into this week's game, Baltimore has lost three straight games. Following their impressive 4-1 start, the Ravens are just 4-4 at this point in time. Obviously, the team's playoff hopes are very much in danger. Baltimore's hopes of winning a Super Bowl seem all but over. No one can fully count the Ravens out, but things are looking bleak. A win over Jacksonville would be a huge step towards getting back on track. On the other hand, a fourth straight loss would put Baltimore in a very difficult situation. Kickoff tonight is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to watch the game on Prime Video.

The 33-10 loss to the Jaguars has raised a lot of questions about the team's offense, and Baltimore now faces a diminished 5% chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic's playoff simulator. Reacting to the Ravens' fifth loss of the season to the Jaguars, former NFL offensive guard Willie Colon on the "Good Morning Football" show on Friday expressed his disappointment with the team's lack of fight and intensity on both sides of the ball. The Super Bowl XLIII winner also questioned whether the offensive line could turn things around with the arrival of quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. "I think the Ravens right now, as they push forward, you just want to see a lot more fight and pride. And they didn't really get that through all both sides of the ball. But right now, man, it's dark days for the Baltimore Ravens," Colon said (1:02 Timestamp). The Baltimore Ravens are now playing without two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson against the backdrop of the quarterback suffering a potentially season-ending thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills. Their initial backup quarterback, Tyler Huntley, is also out for the season after he sustained a toe injury in the same game as Jackson. The Ravens have finalized a trade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals to address some of the offensive issues the team is currently facing. Baltimore Ravens' Quarterback Depth Chart Ahead Of Week 10 After starting their 2026 NFL regular season campaign with four wins in their first five games, the Baltimore Ravens are currently in the midst of a four-loss slump with no visible way out due to injuries to star quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley. While the Brissett trade clearly seems like a contingency plan the Ravens wouldn't have thought of prior to the season, head coach Jesse Minter must devise a foolproof plan for his offense in their Week 10 encounter against the Los Angeles Chargers if they still want to keep their playoff hopes alive. While it remains to be seen who starts for the Ravens at quarterback in Week 10, their depth chart shows undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as starter. Quarterback Austin Reed and new addition Jacoby Brissett are named as the team's second and third-string quarterbacks, respectively. The Ravens' 23-point loss to the Jaguars in Week 9 saw Fagnano start for them, and it won't come as a surprise if Minter decides to change things up, potentially bumping up Brissett as the new starter. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Message to Ravens Revealed in NFL Rumors amid Injury, Return Buzz and Losing Streak
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive. Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field. The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts. Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year. The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game. Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury. A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead. It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

home.blurb: But the Ravens think otherwise, telling teams that Henry is not available before the Nov. 10 deadline, per ESPN . Jackson dealt with a high-ankle sprain before a much-needed return last week against the Buffalo Bills . However, on his first snap of the game, his throwing hand collided with Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau’s hand. He was placed on the injured reserved after needing surgery to repair his thumb. So, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley had to resume his role as the team’s starter, doing so in the games Jackson missed earlier in the season. But Huntley suffered a turf toe injury in the same Bills matchup, knocking him out for the remainder of the season. That led to emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano, a rookie out of UConn, taking over in a 36-10 loss to the Bills. The Ravens made the move to trade for Brissett after the Arizona Cardinals benched him in the second half of a comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8, where head coach Mike LaFleur gave the reins to Gardner Minshew, and later named rookie Carson Beck his backup entering Week 9. The Baltimore Ravens ’ playoff hopes are teetering amid quarterback injury issues and a four-game losing streak, which includes a 33-10 rout by the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. While Baltimore did trade for Jacoby Brissett to hopefully put an end to their signal-caller woes, rumors have begun swirling around one of the team’s stars: running back Derrick Henry . The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday, and some were of the belief the Ravens would at least listen to trade offers for the 32-year-old veteran back – a team that could be one piece like Henry away from a complete squad ready for a Super Bowl run. The speculation surrounded two of Henry’s former head coaches, with John Harbaugh and the New York Giants reportedly in the aggressive buying stage, and running back is where they seem to be looking. The Giants are among those very interested in Jonathan Taylor with the Indianapolis Colts. New England Patriots’ Mike Vrabel could’ve also been a good spot for a Henry reunion, especially given that TreVeyon Henderson was just hospitalized after suffering "unexplainable" neurological symptoms. Henry is a key cog in making this Declan Doyle-led offense work for the Ravens, but it hasn’t looked that way among recent quarterback injuries, most notably to two-time MVP Lamar Jackson. But Brissett’s arrival in Baltimore wasn’t going to come before "Thursday Night Football" against a very good Jaguars team. With steady rain coming down, the Ravens’ offense couldn’t get anything going with Fagnano under center, and now the team hopes Brissett can keep them competitive enough to battle for a playoff spot. There is still a chance Jackson will be returning post-thumb surgery, but he’s forced to miss the next four games on the IR. home.headline: Lamar Jackson told Ravens he’s coming back this season, report says
home.blurb: Injured quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return later this season, the NFL Network reported Sunday, citing anonymous sources. NFL Network reported that Jackson is undergoing surgery to repair a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand. Jackson’s injury typically takes at least six weeks to recover from, though it could take up to nine weeks, the report said. That would line up with a potential return during the Ravens’ four straight AFC North matchups to end the regular season, beginning Dec. 20 at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Perhaps the Ravens still have hope. “Just stay alive” was the paraphrase of Jackson’s message that he delivered within 24 hours of suffering a significant thumb injury on his throwing hand against Buffalo, the report said. After starting 4-1 with Jackson under center, Baltimore has slipped to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North, facing long odds to make the postseason. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on the offense’s first play of his first game back from an ankle injury in a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury against Buffalo, were placed on injured reserve before Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , meaning they will miss at least four games. Jackson has not spoken to reporters since the injury, and coach Jesse Minter has declined to share details about it or Jackson’s potential recovery timeline. “I’m not going to speak on that,” Minter said when asked about Jackson on Thursday night. The Ravens have made plans to move forward without their two-time NFL Most Valuable Player this season, acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. Though neither side disclosed the terms, Baltimore is reportedly sending Arizona a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for the 33-year-old veteran and a 2027 fifth-round selection, ESPN reported. Brissett has started 73 of 109 games and completed 62.1% of his passes with 86 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. He also has 17 career rushing touchdowns. He is 23-50 as a starter. The move came about 12 hours after Baltimore’s embarrassing loss to the Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and struggled mightily with a heavily bandaged right ankle. He completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards and was intercepted twice. Brissett will have time to get up to speed on the offense, with the Ravens not playing again until their Nov. 16 Monday night home game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Have a news tip? Contact C.J. home.blurb: In the same report, Dan Graziano noted the Ravens will "work to solve the problem" with Jackson out for the time being and are "open to a number of ideas" at the quarterback spot with Jacoby Brissett cited as someone they could "look into" acquiring. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars. It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race. Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some of the options the Ravens are looking at include Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent. Jackson returned on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after missing three games then injured his thumb on his first pass attempt. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The Bears may not be eager to trade Bagent since Caleb Williams has already missed time this season, though they did get one quality start from Case Keenum during Williams' absence that might make head coach Ben Johnson comfortable if he had to step in. The Colts are reportedly open to trading Jonathan Taylor, but they still played him 38 offensive snaps and risked a potential injury in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew will remain the starter going forward and rookie Carson Beck will be the No. 2, leaving Brissett as the emergency third quarterback. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. This is so far the most efficient season of Burrow's stellar career, which is a pleasant development of an offense that missed him dearly when he missed a combined 16 games over the last three seasons due to injuries. The Falcons kept Purdy in check when they upset him and the San Francisco 49ers two weeks ago, but Burrow presents an even greater challenge and has a healthier supporting cast than the one Purdy brought into the Week 7 contest. Falcons vs. Bengals prediction Fans of American football in Spain are in for a treat, because this game has all the makings of a shootout. There is not an offense in the NFL that is clicking quite like the Bengals over the last three weeks, and between Burrow, Chase, Higgins, London and Robinson, five of the biggest names in football will be in action in a star-studded battle. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . should bounce back from last week's dreadful 8-for-24 showing in the rain, so Atlanta ought to have enough juice to keep pace with a team that is averaging 36.3 points per game since Oct. 11. In a matchup where points will be aplenty, the team with the better defense holds the edge. It is not as though Atlanta is vastly superior on that side of the ball, but it is much more reliable and is about to insert one of its projected top producers into the lineup for the first time this season. There is not a more opportune time for a disruptive pass rusher like Pearce to make his first appearance than against arguably the best quarterback in the NFL. That alone could be the difference in a high-variance matchup like this one. Atlanta is looking to get back into the win column against a Cincinnati team that has won three consecutive games. The Bengals present a difficult challenge for Atlanta, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Joe Burrow leads one of the NFL’s most productive offenses, featuring star wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. With injuries beginning to catch up with the Falcons , slowing down Cincinnati’s passing attack could be a major challenge. Atlanta’s offense will also need to deliver a strong performance against a Bengals defense that has struggled at times this season. Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson will be important pieces as the Falcons attempt to keep pace with Burrow and company in what could be a high-scoring international matchup. Here are the Falcons On SI staff’s predictions for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup. Garrett Chapman (4-4) The Falcons will have a difficult test on Sunday with the high-flying Bengals offense. They will score plenty of points in this one, and it will be on Michael Penix Jr. to match that production. Working in their favor is the fact that the Bengals are not an elite pressure team, so if they can keep the quarterback clean, then the Falcons could keep up. Atlanta usually wins one of these games they aren’t supposed to every year, and I think Atlanta can find a way to get to Joe Burrow a few times. It’ll be a high-scoring game, and the Falcons’ season survives one more week with a 34-30 win. Prediction: Falcons 34, Bengals 30 Gerald Thomas, III (3-5) Welcome to another week of the most unpredictable team in football. This game has all the makings of one the Falcons play up for. International game, and the Bengals have been rolling with three-straight wins. This game could make for fireworks. Cincy is pretty much the middle of the pack defensively, but has one of the top offenses in the league. So the Falcons will have opportunities to put points on the board too. But can their secondary keep up with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins? We have to wait and see if they prove it. Expect a high-scoring affair in Madrid, with the Bengals coming out victorious. Prediction: Bengals 38, Falcons 34 Darius Hayes (3-5) After picking the Falcons to win each of the last three games, I’m finally going against Atlanta this week. I believed the Falcons had opportunities to pick up wins in two of those matchups, but unfortunately, I was wrong. Heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bengals, I think Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offense will be too much to handle, especially with Atlanta’s injuries beginning to catch up with them. I expect the Falcons to keep it close, but ultimately, I’m taking the Bengals to win 27-24. Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 24 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-5) As inconsistent as the Falcons are, they’ve consistently shown us that they will beat teams they have no business beating and lose to teams they have no business losing to. That makes this a great week to be playing one of the better teams in the league. Pattern recognition aside, there are several aspects of this matchup that make me hopeful. The obvious key to this game will be whether the Falcons can stop Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. But the Falcons have been one of the better pass defenses in the league; they now have a fully healthy secondary, and their best pass rusher is back from suspension, although he is questionable for Sunday. The offense will need a big bounce-back to pull off the upset. Michael Penix Jr. will try to rebound after his best Desmond Ridder impression last week. However, all is not fixed in less than a year. The team on the field remains maddeningly inconsistent because of talent and depth problems inherited by Cunningham and head coach Kevin Stefanski. The Falcons have the same record that I do when trying to predict the outcome of their games: 3-5. In each of their three wins, I've picked them to lose. So naturally, being an underdog in a foreign country is the type of game that makes the Falcons dangerous for Cincinnati. That said, I'm a creature of logic, and logic tells me the cracks in Atlanta's defense will be too much for the offense to overcome. Joe Burrow, Bijan Robinson The Cincinnati Bengals pack their bags for a historic international clash as 3.5-point favorites against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 9, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET at the iconic Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. While Cincinnati rides a three-game winning streak into this matchup behind Joe Burrow's red-hot play, our top Bengals vs. Falcons predictions and NFL picks examine whether the Falcons' feisty secondary can limit big plays, opening up prime betting edges on Tee Higgins as the Bengals look to extend their momentum across the pond. Here are my best bets and NFL picks ahead of Sunday, Nov. 8. Bengals vs Falcons prediction today: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. home.blurb: Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was a full participant Friday, meaning he missed zero actual practice time this week for the Bengals. Turner left during Sunday's win against the Tennessee Titans and was classified as day-to-day with his heel injury to start the week. Defense end Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) is the lone game-time decision Cincinnati will make Sunday. Johnson was a full participant Friday, but it was his only full practice of the week. He left the Titans game and did not return. If Johnson doesn't play, it will leave the Bengals very thin at DE. Rookie Cashius Howell was placed on I.R. before the team left for Madrid . Isaiah Foskey could be elevated from the practice squad to soften the blow. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is the only Bengal confirmed to be out. He aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Five Falcons are officially questionable for Sunday, including DE James Pearce Jr. (back), who went limited Friday after a back injury flared up for him. Atlanta will monitor his status throughout the weekend. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) is out, along with running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring). Former Bengals RB Khalil Herbert has been elevated off the Falcons practice squad in each of the last two games as starter Bijan Robinson's backup. He could get the call once again against his former team. away.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
away.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. The vibes are certainly low in the Colts' locker room, and some "business decisions" could be made on Sunday. Dallas Cowboys injury update before Week 9 game vs. Indianapolis Colts

away.headline: Cowboys vs. Colts prediction: Odds, expert picks, QB matchup, injury update, betting trends, and stats
away.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Jets: NFL Week 9 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On the heels of consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs are back at home and have a lighter game in the 12:00 p.m. local slot against the New York Jets. Just because New York doesn't have the makings of a playoff contender doesn't mean it can't give Kansas City a fight, though. The Chiefs know as well as any team that self-inflicted errors are the easiest way to hand a game over, so the hosts will have to put the pedal to the metal in order to secure a resounding triumph. With kickoff just hours away, will it be the Chiefs or Jets that emerge with a victory? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 9 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: While there's only so much the Chiefs can truly prove against the 2-6 Jets, this is a game Kansas City simply has to win. A two-game losing streak to a pair of playoff teams is one thing. A home loss to a franchise that’s still a year away from even making the “in the hunt” playoff graphic? That would be disastrous. I’ll be watching to see if the Chiefs’ pass rush can wrangle Geno Smith, who is tied for the second-most sacks taken among quarterbacks this season, while hoping to see more from rookie R Mason Thomas in that effort. Will the Chiefs’ banged-up defense be able to hold down a lively group of weapons, even without Garrett Wilson, or will the KC offense need to score more than 24 points for the first time since before the bye week? I could see a bounce-back stat line for Kenneth Walker with another explosive play or two from the star running back. Jordan Foote: The Chiefs typically have at least one game a year they have no business losing and somehow just don't seem to show up for. While it's possible that this is the one, it absolutely cannot be the case. Coming off ugly losses to the Seahawks and Broncos (for different reasons), this is a squad that desperately needs to rebound in a hurry. Fortunately, the matchup is there in Week 9. The Jets' offense has had its shining moments, although it's virtually impossible to trust this version of Smith to go toe-to-toe with Patrick Mahomes if he's on his game. Add in that Kenneth Walker III may be due for another statement performance, and it's hard to see anything other than turnovers or penalties making this too close of a game, in my view. Tyler Brown: The Jets have been more competitive than their 2-6 record suggests, with five of their six losses coming by one score, and Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise. They can be dangerous on offense, with wideouts Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell playing well lately and running back Breece Hall returning, even as Braelon Allen's rushed for 565 yards. This is also a real test for tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore, who will face pass rushers David Bailey and Will McDonald IV. On the other hand, New York’s defense has been giving up production to opposing tight ends, which sets up Travis Kelce and Noah Gray well. Andy Reid can wear the Jets down with Kenneth Walker and, in a perfect world, let Patrick Mahomes work the secondary off that. Smith is also among the league’s worst at turning pressure into sacks, so a Chiefs pass rush that's been waiting for a game like this should hypothetically get home a few times. Neither team will run away, and the Jets will stay in it for a while. But Kansas City is the more talented team and needs the win more. The Chiefs have a stretch of must-win games ahead, and they find a way to handle this one. Published 17 minutes ago JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. The two AFC opponents will meet on the gridiron for the first time since 2023 as KC returns to Arrowhead Stadium following a road stretch. Kansas City will be motivated on both sides of the ball after surrendering a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to the Broncos. Now that the Chiefs no longer hold the lead in the AFC West, every game from here on out is crucial to staying alive in the division race. Meanwhile, the Jets are merely playing for draft position at this stage of the season, having lost six of their past seven matchups and presumably looking to sell a few key pieces at the trade deadline. However, head coach Aaron Glenn is also trying to preserve his job security and convince ownership he's the right man for the job. While sportsbooks favor the Chiefs in this one, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model projects one day before kickoff. Jets at Chiefs: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction It shouldn't come as a surprise that the matchup predictor heavily favors the home team in this one. East Rutherford, NJ October 1, 2023 Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes gets out of the grasp of Quinnen Williams of the Jets in the second half. The New York Jets host the Kansas City Chiefs at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ on October 1, 2023. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 80.2%, Jets 19.7%. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 80.2%, Jets 19.7%. With a greater than four-in-five chance to come out victorious, oddsmakers are heavily backing the Chiefs tomorrow. Chiefs on SI's Take The matchup predictor is correct to side with Kansas City, but the final score shouldn't be as lopsided as many people expect. Chiefs fans might be surprised to learn how competitive the Jets have been in their losses. Five of their six defeats have been decided by one possession, and their biggest margin of defeat was 11 points back in Week 4. Even if the outcomes haven't gone their way, Glenn still has this group playing hard week in and week out. Patrick Mahomes and the defense have taken care of sub-.500 opponents thus far, compiling a 3-0 record in those contests. However, players have openly discussed how difficult it has been to blow out these perceived inferior teams and dominate from start to finish. Many of NY's woes have been pinned on poor coaching decisions rather than a lack of talent. Of course, being without wide receiver Garrett Wilson will greatly impact the Jets' offense for the worse as he continues to be the subject of trade talks . Fans attending the game at Arrowhead tomorrow should feel fairly confident in a Chiefs win, but don't be surprised if the Jets keep it close for a couple of quarters. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Chiefs will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 9.5 points. The game has an over/under of 46.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Chiefs are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can at least pull off one of those infamous moral victories and keep the game competitive against a Chiefs team that may understandably have trouble getting up for a game against the hapless Jets. home.headline: Chiefs reunion in doubt: Hill’s stalled recovery, civil verdict cloud NFL future; Kansas City weighs options
home.source: The Times of India on MSN
home.blurb: Tyreek Hill's injury recovery puts NFL return plans on hold The Chiefs could benefit from another proven receiver, particularly after injuries affected their available options. However, Hill is not the only name under consideration. Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs has also emerged as a potential target. There is another issue the organisation must consider before bringing Hill back. In October 2026, a civil jury found him liable on two battery claims involving his estranged wife. The verdict adds to the questions surrounding his potential return. Tyreek Hill once made the Kansas City Chiefs' offence one of the most feared units in the NFL. Now, the possibility of seeing him back in a Chiefs uniform is becoming harder to imagine. The 32-year-old wide receiver is still waiting for his next opportunity after leaving the Miami Dolphins, but his recovery has not gone as smoothly as hoped. With Kansas City exploring other ways to strengthen its receiving corps, Hill faces a race against time to prove he can still compete at the highest level. His agent's cautious approach now looks increasingly justified. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! Miami eventually released Hill in February 2026, ending a chapter that began with his blockbuster arrival from Kansas City in 2022. His scheduled $51 million salary-cap hit also made his situation difficult for the Dolphins. Agent Drew Rosenhaus has maintained that Hill should not rush his recovery simply to secure another contract. That decision could prove important as teams assess whether the veteran can still deliver at his previous level. NFL reporter Pete Sweeney recently discussed Kansas City's interest during an appearance with Trey Wingo. He suggested the Chiefs could explore several options before making a decision. "I think the Chiefs will try to turn over every stone to try and get a quality receiver." However, Hill's physical condition remains a major concern. Sweeney also explained the timeline that had been discussed locally. "We had kind of heard locally that Tyreek Hill wouldn’t really be ready to pass a physical, take the field until early to mid November." Chiefs reunion faces competition and off-field concerns Sweeney acknowledged that Kansas City must weigh those concerns alongside Hill's football ability. "It's the type of player as well that it's ‘do we want to bring this player into the locker room?’ Just considering some of the off-the-field stuff, but at a certain point, the Chiefs showed us two weeks ago the off-the-field to them maybe doesn’t matter," Sweeney said. Hill finished his injury-shortened 2025 campaign with 21 catches, 265 receiving yards and one touchdown in four games. Until he proves his knee can withstand NFL demands, his comeback remains uncertain. A reunion with Mahomes and the Chiefs is still possible, but Kansas City has little reason to rush its decision. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 9 matchup with Miami. Christian Booher The Detroit Lions have had to navigate some uncharted territory emotionally after the injury to linebacker Jack Campbell. A leader of the defense, Campbell's absence will be tough to account for as he had a huge impact on the operation. While Derrick Barnes is a veteran with plenty of experience, he could need some time to adjust to the new role he's expected to be in. However, I think Dan Campbell's mettle as a motivator will be tested. He was adamant about the importance of remaining focused amidst the adversity, and I think he'll have the team ready to go. They could start slow, but I expect that the offense will get it together quickly. Even with some injuries on the defensive end, the Lions are able to get enough stops to earn a victory in Sunday's game. Lions 38, Dolphins 27 Yes, the Lions will be playing without multiple core defenders on Sunday in Miami (i.e. Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum). And sure, Detroit could be looking ahead to its highly-anticipated Week 10 clash with the New England Patriots in Germany. However, I don't think any of that will matter in the Lions’ Week 9 contest with the 1-6 Dolphins. Yes, Miami is likely better than that record indicates. Yet, Detroit, even with the various injuries, is still the superior team, and I believe will show that early and often on Sunday. Deploying their “next man up” mantra, the Lions pull out a gritty win on the road against the Dolphins. Lions 31, Dolphins 20 John Maakaron The Detroit Lions are hoping to avoid an emotional letdown for multiple reasons. The team is coming off a tough victory against a division rival in the Minnesota Vikings. Unfortunately, linebacker and defensive captain Jack Campbell will be out of action for the foreseeable future after being carted off the field last week. Some may think the Dolphins are a trap game, but Dan Campbell's squad should rally and find the resolve needed to come away with the victory this week. Campbell's injury may also galvanize the roster beyond Week 9, similar to how the 1991 team rallied after Mike Utley suffered a serious injury. Detroit's offense should be able to move the football up and down the field against a young Dolphins team that is still learning how to close out games and win with a new head coach. Tight end Sam LaPorta could be targeted heavily this week, as the Dolphins' defense has given up plenty of yards to opposing tight ends on a weekly basis. Lions 24, Dolphins 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the Miami Dolphins, which were not projected to be that great this year. So far, the Dolphins have met that expectation, ranking among the worst in the league. However, that screams “trap game,” especially with the Munich game next week and the Lions’ minds obviously and rightfully elsewhere with the Jack Campbell injury. The key to the game here is to force more turnovers with quick pressure and to stuff the run game, as the Lions are missing three expected contributors from their linebackers room alone. Led by first-year head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins have struggled to do much right in 2026. Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory . picks.blurb: Roundtable: Previewing Lions Week 9 Matchup Against Dolphins Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 9 matchup with the Miami Dolphins. 1. Do you see any chance of a letdown against Dolphins? Christian Booher: I think with the emotions that have been felt throughout the week, there is a chance that the Lions come out sluggish against Miami. The Jack Campbell injury has been tough for many to process given how severe it was, and the Lions will be without a key player within their defense. His absence will have a big impact, and as a result the defense in particular could struggle. Still, Dan Campbell has proven to be one of the league's best motivators. Because of that, I think the Lions will come out with plenty of fire against the Dolphins. Vito Chirco: Even with all the injuries, I just don't see it. I think Miami is a bit better than its 1-6 record indicates, based on how close it's been in a variety of its losses this season. However, that doesn't mean the Jeff Hafley-led team is going to surprise Dan Campbell's squad on Sunday. I still believe Detroit plays more than well enough to emerge victorious in the Week 9 contest. Emmett Matasovsky: I think there is very much a chance, but I am not saying it is a high one, mind you. The Lions have had an emotional week with Jack Campbell’s injury, and this Dolphins team is one that gets overlooked in the stretch. Additionally, Malik Willis being a mobile quarterback always makes this a potential trap game for Detroit, given its struggles in the Campbell era with mobile quarterbacks. 2. Can Jack Campbell’s injury actually serve as a rallying cry this year for the Lions? Booher : I do think the team will rally around Campbell, and we've already started to see elements of that this year. Campbell was a captain of the defense and a massive leader in the locker room. He leaves big shoes to fill for the time being, but I think the Lions will embrace the challenge and they do have the depth to navigate this injury. Chirco : Yes, I believe it could have that effect. It doesn't take away from the fact that the Lions still need to make a move or two to upgrade their defense. But yes, I believe that Dan Campbell and the players will use Jack Campbell's injury as an extra source of motivation the rest of the way this season. Matasovsky : I absolutely think it can. Campbell is a leader for this locker room and one of the most productive members on defense. The linebacker’s presence will be sorely missed, but the unity in the team at this time can also lead to a more close-knit locker room and better performance. That said, it is not going to be easy to replace the veteran backer, especially with the injuries to Devin White and Jimmy Rolder both factored in. There are not many players with experience in Kelvin Sheppard’s system left. 3. Who do you think the Lions must land at trade deadline? Booher : The Lions need to get a cornerback. D.J. Reed is out Sunday, so the team will get a long look at its depth throughout the game. If things don't go well, it will further amplify the need for general manager Brad Holmes and company. Of the options expected to be available, I think Riq Woolen is the best fit for the defense. He has high-level experience having won a Super Bowl last year, and can be extremely good in Detroit's scheme. Donte Jackson of the Los Angeles Chargers is another good veteran option, though he has had some injury issues this year. Chirco : I'd like to see the Lions make a move for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker. But because of the draft capital that would likely be involved to land Baker, I don't envision it being very likely. That's why I'm going to say Detroit GM Brad Holmes must go out and land Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen. Woolen would be a solid acquisition for Detroit's secondary and provide the organization with a capable No. 2 corner behind D.J. Reed. If I'm Holmes, I'm targeting Woolen leading into Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Matasovsky : A true impact corner, and for me, the ideal target is Riq Woolen from the Philadelphia Eagles. Another much more expensive option would be Sauce Gardner from the Indianapolis Colts, although I am not sure if I see the returns outweighing multiple first round picks. A shutdown corner alongside a healthy Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch makes things scary for opposing offenses, and that is before a healthy DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Aidan Hutchinson are chasing quarterbacks down. 4. Who will be Lions game MVP against Dolphins? Booher : I think the defense will come up big in Sunday's game. With Campbell out, they'll be motivated to produce to show support for their injured teammate. Because of that, I think Aidan Hutchinson will lead the charge and get after Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. I think Hutchinson sets the tone with an early sack and generates a turnover with a strip-sack later in the game to help fuel the team to a win. Chirco : I'm going to go with Jameson Williams, who has scored each of his five touchdowns over the course of the last three weeks. With Amon-Ra St. Brown a bit banged up, I believe that Williams will put together another strong effort and record his fourth straight game with a TD reception. Matasovsky : I think Jahmyr Gibbs will be the game MVP. Sonic is going to get his yards, and this is not a defense that could compete with any NFC North offense on a good day, let alone a mostly healthy Lions offense. Gibbs is going to top 100 yards by the midway point of the third quarter and finish at 175 total yards on the day, if I predict. 5. Which NFC team concerns you the most right now? Booher : There are a pair of teams that I think match up well with the Lions and could give them some fits. One is the San Francisco 49ers. When they're clicking, the 49ers are a tough team to beat due to their array of weapons such as running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. I also think the Bears could give the Lions some fits. Ben Johnson is one of the best offensive minds in football, and Caleb Williams has been playing at a very high level. That Thanksgiving matchup is looming, and could have massive divisional stakes. Chirco : It's the Bears with Caleb Williams, Jeffery Simmons and the great collection of talent they've assembled. They are the one team that might be better than the Lions in the NFC North, which adds further intrigue to their Thanksgiving Day clash with Ben Johnson's team. Matasovsky : It’s the NFL, so any given Sunday. Mostly kidding. On a real note, the San Francisco 49ers look dominant and just re-acquired DeForest Buckner, which makes them a massive threat. If Brandon Aiyuk pays his fines and is in condition to play, they gain another weapon on offense, too. It is going to be hard to get through that San Francisco team, and they are my midway pick for the NFC representative in the Super Bowl thus far. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Lions are 6.5-point favorites over the Dolphins on the spread, with the total set at over/under 50.5 points. Detroit is a -298 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Miami is a +240 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Lions vs Dolphins predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 8. Lions vs Dolphins Prediction Lions vs Dolphins pick: Dolphins +7 (-110) My Dolphins vs. Lions best bet is Miami to cover the spread. Lions vs Dolphins NFL Odds Lions vs Dolphins spread : Lions -6.5 (-112), Dolphins +6.5 (-108) Lions vs Dolphins total : over/under 50.5 (-110o / -110u) Lions vs Dolphins moneyline : Lions -298, Dolphins +240 Lions vs Dolphins NFL Week 9 Preview Detroit Lions Preview: Too Injured to Win by Margin The Lions defense has vastly improved as of late, but the injury bug has once again completely decimated that side of the ball. Star linebacker Jack Campbell went down with a scary neck injury, Kerby Joseph has looked good in practice but still isn't ready, and No. 1 cornerback DJ Reed missed practice all week and has been ruled out. The Lions are suddenly back to a hodgepodge of highly questionable players rotating through the back end of their defense. The only thing this defense currently does well is generate quick pressure. That becomes less of a factor when facing a mobile quarterback who can buy time and extend plays outside the pocket — like Malik Willis. It is difficult to win by margin and cover a full touchdown on the road when you are fielding a bottom-tier defense missing this many crucial pieces. Miami Dolphins Preview: Better Than the Market Indicates The Dolphins offense has shown some juice lately and is playing much better than the market indicates. Since Week 5, Malik Willis ranks 12th in the NFL in adjusted EPA per play and fifth in overall Success Rate. Miami also boasts one of the most explosive rushing attacks in the entire league, ranking No. 2 overall even when adjusting for opponent strength. Malik Willis has been using his legs more while Ollie Gordon has stepped up admirably in place of De'Von Achane. With guard Ryan Proctor looking good to return from a concussion, the trenches will be solidified. Lions vs Dolphins Picks, Betting Analysis Malik Willis has the mobility to negate Detroit's pass rush. He can buy time in the pocket and eventually hit his receivers downfield against a depleted Lions secondary. We might also get some classic Miami rain to slow down the outdoor version of Jared Goff , which isn't nearly as good when he gets to play in a dome. When factoring in all of Detroit's injuries on the back end, my true number on this game is closer to Lions -5. I am happy to take a full touchdown with a Miami offense that has found a successful rhythm. After getting blown out in their first three games of the season, the Dolphins haven't lost a game by more than seven points over their last four contests. Campbell, 26, did not appear to be moving while he was taken off the field, as his teammates looked on with tears and concern. Campbell said Wednesday he is still working on regaining movement in his body, though he does have full movement in his lower body at this time. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he said in a statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger.” Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions lays on the ground after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Mike Mulholland via Getty Images “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he added. “I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Dan Campbell, head coach for the Detroit Lions, previously spoke about visiting Campbell in the hospital, though he declined to share the specifics of his injury or his progress. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said during a press conference on Monday. “Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. away.headline: Is Amon-Ra St. Brown playing today? Lions Week 9 injury report with WR questionable
away.blurb: The Detroit Lions have been rolling of late. Coming out of their bye week, this team has made a statement in the NFC North with wins over the Packers and Vikings. But on Sunday in Week 9, they're going on the road to face the struggling Miami Dolphins. However, one point of concern for the Lions is the fact that star wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was listed as questionable for this game with a ribs injury. That left Lions fans and fantasy managers curious if he was going to be able to play against Miami. St. Brown was limited in practice for the Lions throughout the week, but he's a huge part of what makes this offense work. So everyone concerned with Detroit and their offense heading into Week 9 simply was waiting on Sunday to find out if St. Brown will play this week or not. While St. Brown has been limited all week, reports indicate that the Lions receiver is going to be able to suit up and play against the Dolphins on Sunday. That came from NFL insider Ian Rapoport on Sunday morning. Thus, having him out there in Week 9 is going to be big, even if the level of competition isn't much to write home about. However, given that he was limited in practice and that they're playing the lowly Dolphins, fantasy managers should probably still proceed with a bit of caution when it comes to St. Brown on Sunday. That being said, fantasy managers are obviously still playing St. Brown, but I also wouldn't expect a monster game from the Lions star either. Not only is it a sneaky not-so-easy matchup for the offense in that regard, but the fact that St. Brown was limited all week in practice does make you wonder if we could see Campbell and the Lions coaching staff exercise some caution with his workload and usage in this matchup with so much of the season still laying ahead. This article was originally published on fansided.com as Is Amon-Ra St. Brown playing today? Lions Week 9 injury report with WR questionable . Is Amon-Ra St. Brown playing in Week 9? Lions WR looks ready St. Brown being on the field for the Lions is massively important. He's been such a massive part of the offense for years, the 2026 season being no exception. Through the first seven games of the season, he leads Detroit in targets (76), receptions (53), receiving yards (571) and is tied with Jameson Williams in receiving touchdowns (5). For as much deserved publicity as Jahmyr Gibbs gets as the engine for this offense, St. Brown is a huge cog in making the machine work. home.blurb: Dan Campbell talked up Miami this week not because he's a coach and he's preternaturally paranoid and full of coach speak, but because he's a realist, and he knows the Dolphins, despite their record, have been competitive this season, and he expects they will be again this Sunday. Dave Birkett Rainer Sabin Christian Romo Carlos Monarrez Jeff Seidel Shawn Windsor Detroit Free Press Nov. 8, 2026, 5:04 a.m. ET The Detroit Lions enter their Week 9 matchup with heavy hearts and a sense of purpose. A week after the scary injury to linebacker Jack Campbell that landed him in the hospital, the Lions will take the field trying to make No. 46 proud. And they have a pretty good chance to do so against what is, on paper, an overmatched Miami Dolphins team. The Dolphins (1-6) came into the season as a popular pick to finish last in the NFL and have lived up to those expectations so far. Can the Lions (5-2) take care of business and continue their climb up the NFC standings? Our Free Press experts make their picks: It's been an emotional week for the Lions, and while there will be a crash to pay for it at some point, I don't think that happens now. The Lions are a much more talented team than the Dolphins, even with their injury problems, and the history of teams playing for a teammate who suffers a catastrophic injury on the field are clear. The 2022 Buffalo Bills won their next two games after Damar Hamlin went into cardiac arrest on the field; the 2017 Pittsburgh Steelers won three of four after Ryan Shazier's scary spinal-cord injury; and the 1991 Lions won six straight after Mike Utley was paralyzed. The Dolphins are a scrappy team that's played a bunch of close games of late, but they don't have the guns to compete with the Lions. The pick: Lions 35, Dolphins 17 The Dolphins may be better than their 1-6 record indicates and may show some pluck against an ailing Lions defense, but Detroit knows how much it needs to stack wins against lesser opponents, especially in a division as tough as the NFC North. They'll be prepared, especially if they answer the call to play on behalf of their injured teammate. The pick: Lions 31, Dolphins 24. The Dolphins are in the first year of a rebuild under a new coach. Under normal circumstances, the Lions would be expected to whip Miami. After all, they have won three straight games and just knocked off the last undefeated team, Minnesota. But Detroit is dealing with the fallout from the serious neck injury star linebacker Jack Campbell suffered last Sunday. It’s a challenging situation.
