How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they’ve been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week. Wonnum is still working through the NFL’s concussion protocols and won’t be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it’s unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum’s absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement: Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified. Joseph is looking “better than anticipated,” according to safeties coach Jim O’Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return. The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson's 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken's offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints' defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson's release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore's unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. The Saints are also making their return to New Orleans, which may honestly be bad news for this team. The Saints have been unable to win a game at home this year, and some of their worst performances happened in New Orleans. For a team that has always valued the impact of playing at home, this is a really bad situation to be in, especially given how vocal fans can be. It also doesn't help that the pressure on the coaching staff to perform is palpable. The Saints also made some really important changes before this game. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, and they cut some players, including kicker Daniel Carlson and RB Kendre Miller. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. It starts with the L.A. defense, which is generating a 41% pressure rate on QB dropbacks (third-best in the NFL) and could welcome back Myles Garrett on Sunday to finish those plays. The Commanders had lost three straight before beating up on the short-handed Eagles last weekend — and if the hosts fall behind, it's hard to trust the Washington passing game, which ranks 26th in completion percentage (60.6%) . I'd play this up to -5.5 and 56%. This is a favorable matchup for Williams, who has feasted on 21 red-zone rushing attempts, the sixth-most among all running backs in the NFL. Plus, the Rams' secondary will be depleted without Jaylen Watson — and possibly Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl, too. Look for the L.A. backups to struggle with Diggs' quick release around the goal line. I'd bet this up to 36%. The Rams are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Rams -4.5), with the over/under set at 47.5. Los Angeles is a -225 moneyline favorite while Washington is a +188 underdog. Matthew Stafford's Los Angeles Rams arrive at Northwest Stadium as near-unanimous picks to beat Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders, and our staff went 4-0 for the Rams in this week's picks against the spread . When we added up the straight-up picks from ESPN, NFL.com, Sports Illustrated and CBS Sports' Pete Prisco, 18 of 19 took Los Angeles. The spread picks read differently. Six of the 14 analysts at CBS Sports and Bleacher Report who picked against the number have Washington covering a line that has sat between 4.5 and 5.5 points this week, and the nine analysts who gave a final score average out to a Rams win of 5.8 points, right on top of that number. away.headline: Injuries should have destroyed Rams defense. Instead, they’ve created a monster
away.blurb: “The more you’re out there, the more confidence you get,” he said. “The more I’ve been out there, the more I’m able to make plays and learn from my mistakes as well.” Lake also made something clear: Garrett’s return doesn’t somehow erase the pain of losing Watson. “I still think the magnitude of him going out doesn’t diminish because we got Myles back,” Lake said. “Two completely separate identities.” But this defense didn’t wait for its superstars to get healthy before figuring out how to win. The Rams have lost enough defensive players this season to fill up the foyer of an emergency room, yet somehow, the unit keeps getting better week after week. Maybe that’s the most remarkable part of this roller-coaster season. While injuries have ripped through the roster like a tornado through a trailer park, the Rams’ defense has refused to collapse. In fact, it might be the very thing that saves their season. Three weeks ago, Los Angeles was 2–4, buried in last place in the NFC West and watching its Super Bowl dreams slip away. Now, riding consecutive victories over the Raiders and Chargers, the Rams (4–4) can climb above .500 for the first time this season with a victory over the Commanders on Sunday . And they have their battered defense to thank for it. Consider what happened against the Chargers . The Rams held Justin Herbert & Co. without a touchdown, surrendered nine points and intercepted the quarterback twice. Yes, the Chargers are winless on the season, but that’s not bad for a Rams defense that operated without reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett while losing key starters seemingly every week. Even more impressive? Four Rams cornerbacks finished among Pro Football Focus’ 10 highest-graded players at the position against the Chargers: Trent McDuffie (second), Emmanuel Forbes Jr. (seventh), Jaylen Watson (eighth) and Josh Wallace (10th). That depth in the secondary will be tested again on Sunday in the nation’s capital after Watson, a two-time Super Bowl champion and one of the defense’s emotional leaders, underwent season-ending shoulder surgery after battling repeated dislocations. Wallace and Forbes will now be thrust into bigger roles, but they vow not to use injuries as an excuse. In fact, they don’t seem to be interested in making any excuses. “I’ve been in these shoes before. Been in this position before,” Forbes said of stepping into an expanded role. Wallace echoed that confidence. That mentality starts with leadership. Rams captain Quentin Lake revealed he texted Watson after learning his season was over, reminding him to trust God’s plan. Garrett returned to practice this week for the first time since September and is set to pair with Aaron Donald and Byron Young in what could be the NFL’s most terrifying pass rush. Los Angeles has held four of its last five opponents under 22 points. Its defense ranks fifth in total yards allowed, fourth against the pass and sixth in third-down efficiency. away.blurb: Los Angeles also recently suffered another significant blow when cornerback Jaylen Watson was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a shoulder injury requiring surgery. According to Stick to the Model's injury tracker through Week 8, the Rams have lost $37 million in player value due to injuries, the third-highest total in the NFL. Only the Packers ($42.1 million) and Patriots ($40.3 million) have lost more. The tracker calculates the value lost when a starter misses a game, with each absence costing 1/17 of what that player's grade earns at his position. Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua have accounted for two of the Rams' biggest losses, according to Stick to the Model. Garrett has missed seven games due to a knee injury, while Nacua missed two games earlier this year with a groin injury. Cornerback Trent McDuffie also missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a groin injury. Fortunately, Garrett is at least getting closer to returning from injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in Week 1. Interestingly, the Rams haven't lost nearly as many games from their starters as some other teams. They've had 28 starter games missed due to injury or illness, just above the league average of 25.5 and tied for 12th-most. That makes their third-place standing in player value lost particularly notable. The Rams haven't necessarily had the most absences, but the players they've lost have carried significant value. With Watson now joining the list of season-altering injuries, Los Angeles will have to continue finding ways to overcome the attrition as it pushes through the second half of the season. The 38-year-old made it clear that the soreness had not affected his work or his ability to play. Matthew Stafford speaks out on injury concern Stafford did not appear particularly concerned about the attention surrounding his elbow. away.headline: Rams Midweek Report: A Concerning Trend on Offense, Matthew Stafford's Elbow, and Trade Buzz
away.blurb: Through the first eight weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams’ offense has been productive but inconsistent, to say the least. The Rams rank fourth in yards per game and third in offensive success rate. However, after failing to score 20 points against the Arizona Cardinals before scoring 35 against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams went three-and-out on their first five possessions last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. That was something that a Rams offense hadn’t done this century. There is certainly some context to that as Davante Adams and Puka Nacua have each missed games. Terrance Ferguson has also been out since Week 3. At the same time, the Rams haven’t pushed the ball down the field very often. The Rams have found success out of 13 personnel, but at some point the Rams need to be able to throw the ball. It’s easy to run against inferior teams when the game script is in your favor. However, when that goes south against a true contender, they need to be able to have confidence in their passing game. The eventual return of Ferguson and Adams will help, but is it enough? Two of Matthew Stafford’s 10 lowest single-game averages in intended air yards per attempt have come this season. He has had four straight games averaging under six intended air yards per pass attempt. Over the last four weeks, Stafford has an average depth of target of 5.5 yards, ranking 25 out of 27 quarterbacks. One of the big stories coming out of Sunday’s game was Matthew Stafford being seen leaving the locker room with a bag of ice around his arm. Coincidentally, after not showing up on the injury report all season, Stafford was listed with a right elbow injury this week. Despite Stafford saying he’s fine, this isn’t something to completely sweep under the rug either. It’s well known that Stafford is one of the toughest quarterbacks in the NFL. It will take more than an elbow injury to keep him out. Will Myles Garrett Make His Return Against the Commanders? This week, the Rams opened up Myles Garrett’s practice window . The Rams will now have 21 days to opt to take Garrett off of injured reserve and put him on the active roster. It’s important to clarify that just because the Rams activated Garrett’s practice window, it does not mean he will play on Sunday. His return could still happen after the bye week, as that would be when his 21-day practice window expires. With that said, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier this week that when Garrett gets on the field for practice, it should all happen quickly. The expectation is for Garrett to play this week, but the Rams have prioritized a return to performance, not just a return to play. “It's about that return to performance and a lot of it's going to be predicated on his communication and feedback to us,” McVay said. “Ultimately, being able to see that hopefully the expectation is he's ready to rock this week.” What I will say is that they have called on wide receivers, specifically Josh Downs and Brian T

away.headline: Commanders vs. Rams Friday injury report: Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown out
away.blurb: The Commanders receiver corps is being thinned out by injury. Washington will play Sunday’s game against the L.A. Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report. Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice that the Commanders are concerned about. Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday. TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee. As The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That’s, well, not great. The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve. Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday’s game. Here’s the full Commanders injury report: WR Dyami Brown – Suffered calf injury during Thursday’s practice WR Treylon Burks – Suffered foot injury vs 49ers DT Jer’Zhan Newton – 21-day practice window opened; returning from IR (pec) DL Shy Tuttle – Has a shoulder issue from Week 8 G Sam Cosmi – Dealing with a new knee injury, full practice Friday OT Josh Conerly – Dealing with a new finger issue QB Jayden Daniels – Still listed with Week 2 elbow dislocation TE Colson Yankoff – New knee injury What’s your level of concern with the state of the Commanders injury situation? away.headline: Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl DNP to start Week 9
away.blurb: The Rams released their first injury report of Week 9 on Wednesday and a total of 12 players were listed on it, five of them being non-participants. McDuffie did not practice, nor did Colby Parkinson, Kam Curl or Joe Cardona. McDuffie injured his back last week against the Chargers, Parkinson is still dealing with a rib injury and Curl picked up a foot injury. There is some good news, though. Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Ronnie Rivers were all designated to return and were back at practice. None of them have been activated from IR yet but it's a good sign that they're practicing again. Rivers was a full participant, and Garrett and Ferguson were both limited. There are no other major injury concerns on Washington's side, with three players being limited and three others listed as full – including Daniels with his left elbow injury. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl DNP to start Week 9 Just when it seemed like the Los Angeles Rams were getting healthy, the injury bug bit again . Jaylen Watson is being placed on IR and will miss the rest of the season , and Trent McDuffie is back to missing practice. Matthew Stafford was listed with a right elbow injury but he was still a full participant and he said he's not worried about it, calling the soreness normal for this time of year. The Commanders have dealt with injuries, too, losing Jayden Daniels for a period of time earlier this season and Terry McLaurin for the rest of the year. Only one player missed practice due to injury, and that was Treylon Burks with a foot issue.

home.headline: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out
home.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM "We're still working through those types of things," McVay said Friday morning prior to practice, when asked what kind of ramp-up he expects in terms of how much Garrett is able to play on Sunday. "He's really done a great job in practice. He'll be a DNP today, but it's more of just being smart with him. Nothing to do with anything other than he has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan, and it's been great having him out there, as well as (tight end) Terrance (Ferguson)." While Ferguson (ankle) also returned to practice this week, and was expected to play Sunday according to McVay, he ended up being ruled out after the Rams sent out an updated injury report. Initially listed on this week's report with an ankle injury, Ferguson picked up a hamstring injury in Friday's practice based on the injury updated report. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game, as well as inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which would set up Jake McQuaide to be up from the practice squad again. McVay also said cornerback Jaylen Watson is listed as out, but will be placed on IR. Otherwise, all other Rams players listed on the injury report do not have a game status designation. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out, while defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is listed as questionable. Both players will miss the Week 9 matchup, leaving quarterback Jayden Daniels with fewer passing options. Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only available receivers with game experience at practice, leaving Washington thin at the position for a tough matchup against Los Angeles. Defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable while recovering from a pectoral injury, which could affect Washington's defensive rotation. For the Rams, Brown and Burks' absence creates an opportunity to make Washington's passing attack harder to execute. Limiting the available targets could help Los Angeles focus its defensive attention on Diggs and the remaining receiving options. Myles Garrett Return Could Strengthen Rams Defense The Rams also have positive developments heading into the contest, with star pass rusher Myles Garrett expected to return after missing seven games with a knee injury. They have lost two in a row in ugly fashion, and they risk this devolving into a totally lost season. Unfortunately, the Denver Broncos and their devil magic are coming to town. The Panthers are underdogs. No one seems to be willing to predict an upset this week despite the fact that Denver is travelling across the country after an emotional win. Can the Panthers pull it off in Charlotte? Here's what the Panthers On SI staff thinks. Russell Baxter: Panthers 23, Broncos 21 Five of Denver’s six victories this season have been by seven points or less. And this clash of defending division champions looks like it may be the same. The Broncos have struggled to run and have had issues stopping the run. Look for a 25-plus carry day from Chuba Hubbard, and for the Broncos’ PK Wil Lutz to miss late on a potential game-winning field goal. Zach Roberts: Broncos 20, Panthers 17 Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) during the game against the Green Bay Packers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Don't get me wrong, there is a path to victory. If Brad Idzik can scheme up quick passes or have hot routes available for Bryce Young when pressure comes, because it absolutely will, the offense will be fine and can also lean on Chuba Hubbard with a boatload of carries. Don't get me wrong, there is a path to victory. If Brad Idzik can scheme up quick passes or have hot routes available for Bryce Young when pressure comes, because it absolutely will, the offense will be fine and can also lean on Chuba Hubbard with a boatload of carries. On defense, this is actually a good matchup for the Panthers. The Broncos don't have the guns to take advantage of the cornerback depth issues, and Denver hasn't run the ball terribly well all season. The Panthers' weaknesses won't be taken advantage of. That said, that Broncos defense is really good, and we're not confident Idzik will have the answers all game long. The Broncos have won games they have no business winning all year, and that should continue with some more magic this weekend. Mark Livingston: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 The Panthers have a chance to pull off an upset at home, but their offensive line remains a major concern heading into Sunday’s matchup. Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times over the last two games, and now Carolina faces a Denver defense that has already recorded 23 sacks this season. The Broncos haven’t exactly been lighting up the scoreboard offensively, so Carolina should have opportunities to keep this game close. However, unless the Panthers can protect Young and avoid costly mistakes, Denver will likely make enough plays to leave Charlotte with the win. Preston Palm: Broncos 33, Panthers 24 Carolina is in desperation mode this week after two horrendous losses, and yet they face their toughest test yet. The Broncos are tied for the most wins in the AFC and are elite in one area where Carolina struggles most to counter: the pass rush. Bryce Young has his hands full once again; Denver ranks No. 1 in the NFL in pass rush win rate, PFF pass rush grade, and total QB pressures. Against an offensive line that has been nothing short of abysmal, that matchup could be the deciding factor in the game. Young has to find ways to be productive despite the real possibility of not having any time in the pocket. Denver’s pass defense is exploitable, and their offense is still figuring itself out. With clean pockets, the Panthers can move the ball on this defense, but the Broncos always seem to figure things out as the game gets into the fourth quarter. Carolina hasn’t shown that they can withstand what’s coming from Denver’s pass rush, and that will be the difference. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. The Texans got upset at home by the Giants in their last game, ending a two-game winning streak for Houston. They still have some fight in them, though, despite being 2-5. The same can’t be said for the Chargers, who have yet to cover a spread let alone win a game through their first seven contests. The Texans beat the Chargers 32-12 and 20-16 last season. Let’s take a look at a few prop picks, including an anytime touchdown scorer, for Texans vs. Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8. Best NFL Prop Bets for Texans vs. Chargers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Justin Herbert OVER 0.5 Interceptions (-175) Kayshon Boutte OVER 17.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Woody Marks Anytime Touchdown (+110) Let’s get the juicy play out of the way first: barring an injury, Justin Herbert will throw an interception this week. Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions on the season, with at least one in all seven games thus far. He’s thrown two interceptions in three games, including last week at the Rams. Houston picked off Herbert in the one game against him last year as well. Kayshon Boutte has become a reliable target for C.J. Stroud. The wide receiver only needed one catch on two targets to get 25 yards last week, and has gone OVER 17.5 yards in six of seven games this season. Mind you, that one UNDER was a game in which he had two catches for 16 yards, just missing the mark. This is a prop that can cash on just one play, and the Texans should look to spread the ball around a bit against the Chargers. Woody Marks will get another chance as the Texans starter this week after David Montgomery was ruled out due to injury. He’s yet to score in the two games without Montgomery, but I think that changes this week. The Chargers have allowed a running back to score in six of their seven games this season, including both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum scoring last week. And in this game between two of the NFL's bigger disappointments from the first half of the season, there's due to be a handful of surprises to unravel throughout the course of Sunday's action. Heck, it's a pretty big surprise that these two to have a combined record of 2-12 in the first seven games. So with that in mind, in the hours leading up to Sunday's kickoff in Los Angeles, now feels like the perfect time to sort through a batch of three bold Texans predictions and try and guess some surprising outcomes on how Week 9 might unfold: Woody Marks Totals Over 100 Yards From Scrimmage Dec 27, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Houston Texans running back Woody Marks (27) carries the ball as Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Tarheeb Still (29) defends during the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the time that David Montgomery has been stuck on the sidelines with a lingering groin injury, Woody Marks has been the primary back the Texans have leaned on within their running back room, and he's turned in some solid performances throughout. In the time that David Montgomery has been stuck on the sidelines with a lingering groin injury, Woody Marks has been the primary back the Texans have leaned on within their running back room, and he's turned in some solid performances throughout. Marks has accumulated at least 17 touches and 80 yards from scrimmage over the Texans' past three games. It's resulted in much better production within Houston's ground game compared to the first four games of the year. But this game against the Chargers and their rushing defense is a matchup the Texans and Marks can really expose. Los Angeles has allowed 4.1 yards per carry this season while also ranking within the bottom 10 of rushing attempts, yards, and touchdowns allowed. Teams take a lead on the Chargers and double down on the run game as the game progresses. Those holes in the Chargers' run defense paired with the fact that Montgomery is out once again for Week 9, could set the stage for another big day from Marks–– maybe even for as much as 100 yards from scrimmage. Stroud. But that made for Harrison Jr.'s only reception of the day on four targets against the Giants. Sure, a nice play between Stroud and Harrison Jr., but overall, an underwhelming day for the pairing altogether. Now coming off of a bye, where their new receiver addition has had even more time to learn the playbook and get adjusted with his new team, there's a ton of incentive to get him involved early and often against the Chargers this Sunday. Perhaps that even leads to another touchdown score. I'm anticipating a game with much more Harrison Jr. involvement on the offensive end entirely. And if that increased usage really pans out as expected, then another week of seeing a shot to the end zone from Stroud to his college teammate might not be too hard to imagine. Texans Take Home a 10+ Point Victory Dec 27, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) waves to fans following a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Texans need a cathartic, commanding win like this. The Texans need a cathartic, commanding win like this. Houston's three games under .500, desperately looking to cling onto their hopes of making the postseason. They're fresh off a bye where the entire roster should have legs feeling a little bit fresher, and the hunger to get back on track with a win becomes even greater coming off of their last overtime loss to the Giants. And while the Texans are taking the trip out West to play on the road for this one, the pieces should still be in place for this team to take care of business against the Chargers. The Chargers remain the only winless team left in the NFL through eight weeks. They rank 32nd in the NFL in total points and first in turnovers allowed. Nobody wants to be that team giving Los Angeles their first win of the season, and especially not the Texans with an extra week of rest to prepare . This should be a game where the Texans' defense gets back on track with a couple of turnovers, turns that into good field positioning for Stroud and Co., and puts together a multiple-score victory in hopes of starting another late-season run similar to 2025. Houston looks to keep Los Angeles winless, and my Texans vs. Chargers prediction says the Texans have the edge on both sides of the ball as 5.5-point road favorites. The Chargers own the league's worst scoring offense at 14.1 points per game, and they'll face a Houston pass rush that keeps getting home. Check out my NFL picks for Sunday, Nov. 8, plus our Week 9 best bets for every game, with kickoff set for 4:05 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium on CBS. TOP PICK Texans vs Chargers prediction: Texans -5.5 Play up to 57%. The Houston Texans may be sitting at 2-5, but they're a much better offensive team. Houston is averaging 23.6 ppg (12th) compared to a league-worst 14.1 points per contest for the Los Angeles Chargers , one of the games in our Week 9 against-the-spread picks . I also expect a long day for Justin Herbert , who has already been sacked 23 times. He's up against a Texans pass rush that has the fifth-most sacks in the AFC . Will Anderson Jr. leads the unit with 7.5 sacks. C.J. Stroud , meanwhile, has thrown just one interception this season. Houston has also won both road games this season, and I expect the Texans to cover on Sunday. Texans vs Chargers combo I expect a low-scoring Week 9 affair. Herbert will likely struggle to move the ball, given Houston's success pressuring the quarterback, and LA hasn't scored a touchdown in back-to-back games . Houston has been more productive offensively, but the Texans haven't been particularly consistent either. I expect them to score 20-25 points while limiting the Chargers to 10-14, keeping this contest comfortably Under 40.5 (see our Week 9 Over/Under predictions for every game). Tre' Harris has been one of LA's more reliable targets this season. He has 18 receptions on 29 targets, and the youngster has cashed the Over in three of his last four outings . Houston's secondary isn't great, ranking 28th in passing yards allowed. Tre' Harris Over 2.5 receptions Texans vs Chargers touchdown scorer: Nico Collins Play up to 42%. Nico Collins is second on the Texans in receptions (24) and tied for first in TDs (3). He has five red-zone targets this season with three catches, turning two of those into scores . Stroud frequently targets him, and Collins' physicality is a major strength near the goal line. Even though the Chargers have been particularly solid at defending in the red zone, Collins is my strongest look among Week 9 anytime touchdown picks on Sunday. Texans vs Chargers player prop: Woody Marks 60+ rushing yards With David Montgomery still injured, Woody Marks will be RB1 once again today, and I expect him to flourish. Even though the Texans don't run the football a whole lot, they could resort to putting the ball in Marks' hands more. L.A. is stingy against the pass, but they're 23rd against the run , allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Marks has logged at least 15 carries in each game since Montgomery was injured, and he's cleared this total in two of those games . In the other, he still finished with 56 yards, just a tad below the threshold. He'll be a force at SoFi, making him a strong target among Week 9 player props . Want more NFL player props? Los Angeles remains the only winless team in the NFL. They are certainly one of the league's more disappointing teams, and the Texans are in the same boat. The Chargers (0-7) will host the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. The two teams are nowhere near where they expected to be, but they'll hope this week helps one of them turn the tide. Here are four bold predictions for Week 9. J ustin Herbert throws for 300+ yards and one touchdown Herbert is coming off a season-high 257 passing yards. Los Angeles rushed for 64 yards against the Rams, averaging 2.6 yards per carry. Omarion Hampton could see an increased role in the backfield, with a fierce pass rush led by Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. home.headline: Chargers final injury report before NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and continue to shock the NFL world by showing an unwillingness to trade any of their players despite facing down a lost season in 2026. Los Angeles had hoped to right the ship and gain some momentum coming out of their week seven bye but looked listless against the Los Angeles Rams in week eight. The Chargers do have other players who may be targets on the trade market but so far the word that has been put out to insiders around the NFL is that the Chargers are continuing to execute their plan of standing pat and trying to right the ship before heading into the 2027 season. The return of Donte Jackson to field is intriguing as he has been floated as a possible trade candidate and the Chargers have built up significant young depth both on the roster and the practice squad. The Chargers have been battered by injuries this season. The joke around the NFL may be about the San Francisco 49ers electrical substation and its proximity to the practice facility but someone may need to look into the water in Los Angeles with the amount of injuries both LA teams have faced this season. By week six, the Chargers had over half of their original 53-man roster either on that week's injury report or on injured reserve. The Chargers are already down to their fifth option at left guard and despite hope for getting reinforcements to face the Houston Texans, it appears guard Kayode Awosika, who has not played since week two, is still at least one week away from returning to the field. The Chargers opened the practice windows for tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman this week but it appears that neither are ready to be activated off of injured reserve just yet. The Chargers are set to get some depth at cornerback returning to the field with Donte Jackson and rookie Rodney Shelley clear of the injury report and will carry no injury designation into the game on Sunday. The Chargers front office has been shockingly unwilling to engage with trade calls despite their record generating buzz and demand . The most obvious trade candidate, edge rusher Khalil Mack, has publicly stated that he wants to stay and head coach Jim Harbaugh has echoed that sentiment at the podium. Whether Mack is simply being a consummate professional or he really does not want to uproot and leave his family behind remains to be seen with the trade deadline just days away. If the Chargers lose to the Texans, drop to 0-8 and maintain they are not willing to trade anyone, they might no longer be operating under logic and may be relying on the force. Los Angeles is starting to get some of their injured players back and perhaps, the front office and ownership feel getting the team somewhat stable during the back half of the season and heading into the offseason is more important than a few day three draft picks. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers (+3) at New England Patriots This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Pick: Bills 21, Vikings 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. It’s not who you play but when you play them. The Green Bay Packers will face the New England Patriots on Sunday. It’s a measuring-stick game for the Packers, who believe they are Super Bowl contenders. The Patriots played in the Super Bowl last year and believe they have the goods to take the next step. With a top-tier quarterback and coach and a strong defense, they will be a formidable challenge. The Patriots, however, will play without their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Their premier tight end, Hunter Henry, is questionable with a foot injury that held him out of practice to start the week. Their starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu, are on injured reserve. So is their top pass rusher, Harold Landry. Can the Packers take advantage of the “when you play them” part of that adage? Here are our weekly game predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Patriots Prediction The Packers have had some good fortune this season. They faced the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield and the Bears without Caleb Williams. They will have more good fortune against the Patriots. While Drake Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up, will be the starting quarterback, he’s going to be playing with an incredibly shorthanded group of receivers. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are not the same as A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Good quarterbacks can make it work with whoever, so this won’t be a layup victory for Jonathan Gannon’s defense. However, New England’s pass protection has been leaky, with Maye facing the fourth-highest pressure rate in the league. Can the Patriots’ receivers get open before the Packers’ pass rush arrives on the scene? Added together, the game has been put on a silver platter for Green Bay’s defense to be the most powerful unit on the field. On the other side of the ball, it’s going to be a challenging day for Jordan Love, as well. The Packers, of course, can’t run the football, and it’s having an impact on the passing game with the play-action attack having become irrelevant . If the Packers can’t run the ball – and what reason is there to believe they will? – they’re going to have to deal with the teeth of the Patriots’ strong pass rush, which ranks fifth in sack percentage. Elijah Ponder – the best pass rusher that nobody has ever heard of – is seventh in the league with six sacks. With 3.5 sacks, Christian Barmore powers the interior rush. “He’s a really good player,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of Ponder, an undrafted free agent last year. “To be truthful, I hadn’t heard a whole lot about him until I started watching the tape and I’m like who is this guy? What’s his story? How do we not know about him? Everybody knows about him now. When you look at their edges, all three of those guys that are really doing the bulk of the work are really good players, and you couple that with the interior guys, it’s a really formidable front.” That could mean limited time for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat the premier cornerback duo of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. “Really good DBs,” Love said. “I think they do a lot of things very well. I think as anything, it’s a challenge for me, for the receivers on the outside to be able to go see how good we can be and how good we can attack them and make plays against them. I think they do a really good job. I think Gonzalez is definitely one of the best in the league and he makes plays. I feel like for us, it’s a fun test.” Ultimately, I’m taking the Packers, who are 3-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . Both quarterbacks are really good, but I’ll take Watson and Golden vs. Gonzalez and Davis over Hollins and Douglas vs. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. In a close game, the Packers will fail to run out the clock but the defense will save the day. And they’ll need it, with the Bears and Lions favored to win their games against the Buccaneers and Dolphins, respectively, while the first-place Vikings are underdogs against Buffalo. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 20. Bill’s Record: 6-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Patriots Prediction Everything outside of the field favors New England in this game with the return of Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady, which has been discussed all week. The reality on the field, however, is that the Packers have more healthy players than the Patriots do. The Patriots are missing their top two receivers and their starting tight end is going to be hobbled, at minimum, if he can play. Drake Maye and Jordon Love are both being asked to carry a heavy load, but Love has a better supporting cast around him. In addition, Jonathan Gannon should be able to create enough confusion for Maye to make a couple of mistakes that swing the game in the Packers’ favor. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 17. Jacob’s Record: 5-3. His poise and composure at the line of scrimmage, I think he's worked on cadences, and the operation has really improved from a young quarterback coming out." X-Factor: WR Mack Hollins (if activated) Without A.J. Brown for the second-straight week and Romeo Doubs still on IR, the Patriots continue to deal with a depleted wide receiver room (DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III). If the Patriots choose to activate Hollins off of IR for this game, they'd be able to get some much-needed size back at the position. Hollins hasn't played since Week 4 after dealing with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo, and returned to practice this week. Final Score Prediction: Patriots 28, Packers 23 The Patriots, despite the slow start in Miami a week ago, feel like they're on a roll. In front of a national audience with Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game, I don't see how this week ends in a loss. What it will take is Maye slinging it just like he's done the last few games and use his legs to extend some plays — as well as not letting Green Bay's rushing attack with Josh Jacobs find its footing. On Sunday, the still-injury-riddled Patriots will have to perform to their highest level for a chance to beat a Packers squad with playoff aspirations. On Sunday, the still-injury-riddled Patriots will have to perform to their highest level for a chance to beat a Packers squad with playoff aspirations. New England’s best chance at victory? Forcing Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to make poor decisions. The Packers’ pass-heavy offense averages the second-most yards through the air in the NFL, and the fewest rush yards per game. Green Bay’s 28-year-old signal caller has thrown an interception in each of his past three games, an opportunity New England may need to capitalize on. X-Factor: CB Marcus Jones This season, Green Bay has relied heavily on second-year wide receiver Matthew Golden. The speedy pass catcher sits top-10 in the NFL in both receptions and receiving yards. I expect Jones to play a major part in attempting to slow down the wideout’s production on Sunday. Not to mention, Jones’ other role for the Patriots — punt returner — is one the Packers have stuffed all season long. Green Bay allows the second-fewest yards per punt return in the NFL. From locking down a star wideout to boosting the New England offense’s field position, Jones will play a pivotal role in his team’s success on Sunday. New England hardly had the talent to take down Miami a week ago. With the Patriots’ receiver room still highlighted by DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, it feels hard to believe they can produce enough offensively to squeak out a win. But maybe — just maybe — a Super Bowl LI reunion, Tom Brady being back in Gillette Stadium and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame might just bring the magic New England needs come Sunday. Tom Brady will be in the booth for his former team's Week 9 matchup, and the action at Gillette Stadium promises plenty of drama on the field too as the New England Patriots host the Green Bay Packers. With New England laying 3. 5 points as home favorites and the total set at 44. 5 points, my top Packers vs. Patriots predictions and NFL picks back Green Bay's relentless pass defense to steal the spotlight, keeping this affair close enough for the road underdogs to cover. It all gets started at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. TOP PICK Packers vs Patriots prediction today: Packers +3.5 I'm locking in the Green Bay Packers +3.5, down to +2.5 , because they have better net early-down EPA per play and a higher quarterback-pressure rate differential than the New England Patriots , and I like this matchup for Green Bay's defense. According to RBSDM.com, the Packers rank third in weighted defensive EPA per dropback . Drake Maye struggled against the Seahawks (fifth), Steelers (sixth), and Jaguars (fourth), completing just 63.8% of his passes with one touchdown and six interceptions. Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon also gets extra prep time for a New England offense without wide receiver A.J. Brown and possibly without Mack Hollins and tight end Hunter Henry . Green Bay limits explosives, forcing Maye to work the ball methodically downfield, where we've already seen him make costly mistakes. Packers vs Patriots combo I expect Green Bay to dictate the terms defensively, but that doesn't mean the Packers need to win outright for me to cash. New England can move the chains without producing explosive plays, which helps running back Rhamondre Stevenson pile up receiving yards while keeping the game within one possession. Meanwhile, Green Bay doesn't need a monster offensive performance, either. One well-executed red-zone possession could be enough for tight end Tucker Kraft to find pay dirt. The beauty of this angle is that I don't need either quarterback to light up the scoreboard . In fact, a relatively ugly, low-scoring game could work perfectly fine for all three legs. New England has excellent outside cornerbacks, but the middle of its defense is vulnerable in coverage. Kraft was enjoying a career year before tearing his ACL around this time last season. He hasn't quite regained that form, but he's still a Pro Bowl-caliber tight end . With New England stronger on the outside than over the middle, I like Kraft's chances of finding the end zone. Predicting the Raiders' Week 9 Moves In their Week 8 matchup against the Jets, Las Vegas made several notable changes to their starting lineup that proved fruitful. After struggling to find competent play at the right guard position between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, the Raiders turned to rookie Trey Zuhn. The Jets are not known for being a stout defense, but they are serviceable and gave Las Vegas fits for the entire first half, holding the Raiders to 97 total yards. Still, Zuhn looked like he may be the Raiders' best option at right guard for the rest of the season. Sunday's matchup against the 49ers will be much more telling, as San Francisco's defense is much more of a challenge than New York's. It will be interesting to see how Zuhn does at guard against one of the toughest teams the Raiders will face this season. If Zuhn plays well against the 49ers, the starting right guard position is his to lose. Starting Zuhn at right guard wasn't the only change Las Vegas made against the Jets. They also started rookie running back Mike Washington over Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders cannot afford to sit Jeanty for an entire game, as he is far too valuable catching the ball out of the backfield. Still, the way they successfully used Washington on the ground and Jeanty through the air against the Jets is worth building upon in Week 9 against the 49ers. Ahead of the team's road matchup against the 49ers, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko praised Washington's Week 8 outing. “He’s somebody that continues to improve, really works his craft. He wants to get better at each and every single thing he does, whether it’s fitting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. It’s all the little fundamental things that we talk about. It’s stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that’ll allow him to become a more successful player,” Janocko said earlier this week. “Running the ball is a full team thing. The greatest thing about football in general is that it’s 11 as one on every single play. So, it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful." Cornerback Darien Porter returned to practice this week after playing only one play against the New York Jets last Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable heading into Week 9. However, speed is arguably Porter's greatest asset on the field, and he is dealing with a groin injury. A groin injury can linger. Despite being listed as questionable, Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard may decide not to risk damage to Porter's long-term health in a game where they already face an uphill battle. Las Vegas faced a similar decision earlier this season, when they could have rested running back Ashton Jeanty against a New England Patriots team that was missing more than five players before their matchup ended. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." home.headline: 49ers considering creative offensive upgrade at NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: Demarcus Robinson is coming back, and the 49ers should be able to get Stribling back in December, while Evans and Samuel might return in the near future. George Kittle is obviously great, but Jake Tonges is out for the season, and the 49ers could use some extra depth at the position, especially if it's in the form of a good pass-catching option. Trading for a tight end would be a creative way for the 49ers to improve the offense. There aren't a lot of great options out there, but this report from Schefter and Rapoport indicates this potential trade is very much in play for the 49ers. 49ers considering creative offensive upgrade at NFL trade deadline - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 49ers considering creative offensive upgrade at NFL trade deadline Matt Sullivan · The Sporting News Sun, November 8, 2026 at 3:51 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches, it shouldn't be a surprise that the 49ers are considering a few moves to upgrade their roster. They've already improved their defensive line, so what's next? Considering all of the injuries to the wide receiver position, including the recent placement of Christian Kirk back on IR, adding WR help would make a ton of sense. The 49ers are showing interest in some of the top WR options this season. But, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , they're also considering an interesting and creative alternative to the WR room. Instead, they are looking at the tight end position for an offensive upgrade. 49ers looking to the TE market for a creative trade option "The 49ers are also combing the tight end market, which would be another way to add a pass-catcher if a trade for a receiver doesn't come to fruition," Schefter and Rapoport report. With the 49ers in need of more offensive firepower, wide receiver is an obvious area to target. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De'Zhaun Stribling, and Kirk are all missing time due to injuries right now. All three can come back this season, which would put the WR room in good shape. That could then give the 49ers a reason to acquire a pass-catching tight end. MORE : Jerry Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer after Cowboys collapse vs. Cardinals Someone like Dallas Goedert of the Philadelphia Eagles or David Njoku of the Los Angeles Chargers could make a lot of sense. Those kinds of players would give Brock Purdy another quality pass-catcher to target, while also improving the TE position overall. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Ex-NFL star Antonio Brown avoids jail time as part of plea deal after Miami shooting Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). home.headline: Sam Darnold Injured, Latest Rumors as QB 'in Danger of Missing' More Games for Seahawks
home.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals and reportedly may also be out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders. ESPN's Adam Schefter , citing league sources, reported on Sunday that Darnold "is in danger of missing Seattle's Week 10 game against the Raiders." Schefter added that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . away.headline: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
away.blurb: Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team's previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers' Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team's final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday's contest.
